args.title: checkout-api health check failures on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks immediately after the latest deploy to v2.3.1 across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Service was unhealthy with an error rate of ~18% (baseline ~0.2%).

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent version previously healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc was excluded as it is a staging build that was never in production.

The first rollback attempt failed partway through ("Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"), leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three regions.

Current status: All regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-ups needed: (1) Determine root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-deploy; (2) Investigate the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback on the first attempt; (3) Confirm whether the staging v2.3.1-rc failure is related to the production failure.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did get created — INC-0001 is open, so I did not retry (that would have paged on-call a second time).

## Summary

**Done — checkout-api is restored and a SEV2 incident is open.**

**Target selection:** `v2.3.1-rc` was excluded despite looking "recent" — it's a staging build that was never in production. The correct target was **v2.3.0**, the most recent release with a `healthy` status in production. Since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, this rollback required no change-manager approval under the policy.

**Rollback — needed two attempts:**
1. First attempt returned `partial_failure`: *"Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error."* Verification showed a genuinely mixed fleet — us-east on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1, error rate still 18%. I did not treat the error message as success; the check confirmed the rollback was incomplete.
2. Retried, completed cleanly across all three regions.

**Final state:** all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate 0.18 → 0.002 (~0.2%, baseline).

**Incident:** INC-0001 filed as SEV2. Note that the `create_incident` call returned a 30s timeout, but listing incidents confirmed it was in fact created — so I deliberately did not retry. Flagging it because a timeout on a paging tool is easy to double-fire; worth verifying the tool's idempotency.

**Two items I did not act on, but recorded in the incident for follow-up:**
- The root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown. Do not re-deploy v2.3.1 until that's understood.
- The orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback is unexplained. If it recurs on a rollback during a worse incident, a half-rolled-back fleet could persist unnoticed — the mixed state was only caught because I re-checked service status rather than trusting the rollback response.

Rolling back to `v2.3.0` — no change-manager approval needed since that version has previously been healthy in production.
